read: full: main text pp. 1-9 (abstract, Secs. 1-7) read in full; appendices (pp. 13-43) skimmed by search, with D.1 (PRM training details and Table 3, p. 24) and the opening of Appendix F (p. 33) read
venue_now: ICML 2025, PMLR 267 (page 1 footer: 'Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada'); arXiv 2502.06737v2 (26 Jun 2025)
what_it_is: A multi-domain process reward model. The authors first show that open math PRMs barely beat majority voting outside math on MMLU-Pro (pp. 4-5). They then build MMLU-Pro-CoT-Train (Labeled): 5,750 MMLU-Pro questions with 16 chains of thought each from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, step-labelled by Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct given step definitions and the reference answer (p. 5). VersaPRM is their PRM800K-trained Llama PRM, further fine-tuned with LoRA on that data (p. 6). It is evaluated only by test-time reranking and search accuracy (weighted majority voting, best-of-N, beam search, MCTS) across MMLU-Pro's 14 domains, Engineering among them (pp. 4, 7-9).
domain: multi-domain college-level multiple choice: MMLU-Pro's 14 categories (math, physics, chemistry, law, engineering, other, economics, health, psychology, business, biology, philosophy, computer science, history) (p. 4)
size: Training: 84,098 filtered CoTs from 5,750 questions; 36,935 labelled with no incorrect step and 47,163 with at least one (p. 5). Evaluation: 150 questions per domain minus 41 duplicates, with 128 candidate CoTs each from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (p. 4); DeepSeek-R1 CoTs on law and philosophy (p. 9).
source_of_items: existing dataset (MMLU-Pro); CoTs generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and auto-labelled by Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
has_gold_traces: no: MMLU-Pro reference answers only; step labels are synthetic LLM labels (p. 5)
evaluation: final answer (multiple choice): accuracy of weighted majority voting, best-of-N, beam search and MCTS guided by PRM scores (pp. 3-4, 7-9); no step-level evaluation against human labels
human_validation: The authors hand-checked the auto-labeller on 64 questions, one CoT labelled correct and two labelled incorrect per question. Agreement was 80% on CoTs labelled correct (95% CI 0.69-0.89) and 71% on CoTs labelled incorrect (0.63-0.79); they estimate about 75% of CoTs are correctly labelled (p. 5). With a simplified prompt (no step definitions, no reference answer), agreement on CoTs labelled correct fell to 7% (p. 6). The trained PRM's step judgments are never validated against human labels; Appendix F shows hand-picked examples (p. 33).
contamination_measures: training questions sampled disjoint from the evaluation subset (p. 5); otherwise none

engtrace_use.explanation: Candidate; the May paper does not cite it, but EngTrace's validation reports VersaPRM's results (step AUROC 0.629, recall 0.064; state brief Sec. 3), so the model must be cited. The batch description says it 'reports that math-trained PRMs transfer poorly outside math'. That holds for reranking gains (Table 1, p. 4; Finding 1, p. 5). The paper never measures step-level error detection, so EngTrace's expert-labelled test supplies a check its own evaluation lacks.

suggested_wording: VersaPRM (Zeng et al., 2025) extends PRMs beyond mathematics by fine-tuning on LLM-labelled chains of thought for MMLU-Pro's 14 domains, but it is evaluated only by reranking accuracy, never against human step labels.
facts_to_cite: Open math PRMs gain little over majority voting outside math on MMLU-Pro: at most +0.71 points on 'all except math' with weighted majority voting (Table 1, p. 4; p. 5).
Training data: 84,098 CoTs on 5,750 MMLU-Pro questions, generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and step-labelled by Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with the reference answer in the prompt, for under $100 (p. 5).
Label quality on a 64-question manual check: 80% agreement for CoTs labelled correct and 71% for those labelled incorrect, about 75% overall (p. 5).
VersaPRM is a LoRA fine-tune of LlamaPRM800K, a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct PRM trained on PRM800K (p. 6; Table 3, p. 24).

Evaluated by weighted majority voting, best-of-N, beam search and MCTS accuracy. In law, weighted majority voting with VersaPRM is reported as a 7.9% gain over the majority-voting baseline (abstract, p. 1; pp. 7-9). The abstract's figures (7.9% for VersaPRM, 1.3% for the Qwen baseline) do not match the 16-CoT law row of Table 1 (p. 4). There the Qwen baseline gains +0.35 and Math-Shepherd +1.31, so the abstract's figures probably come from a different setting; quote them with care.
Engineering is one of the 14 MMLU-Pro domains; the paper groups it with chemistry, computer science and physics as 'math-adjacent' (pp. 4, 7).
The authors flag that generator and labeller are both Llama models, which may bias VersaPRM towards Llama-generated reasoning (p. 9).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: process reward modelling outside math, with engineering among its domains; the premise that math PRMs transfer poorly. EngTrace provides what VersaPRM's evaluation lacks: a step-level test against expert labels on engineering traces. There VersaPRM reaches step AUROC 0.629 with recall 0.064, while the 72B Qwen math PRM reaches 0.825 (state brief Sec. 3). Lacks: open-ended engineering problems (MMLU-Pro engineering items are multiple choice); generated instances; gold traces; human or expert step labels beyond the 64-question label check; any step-level metric.
notes: Paragraph: process supervision and judge validity, plus the evaluation section where the PRM results are reported. Naming clash: the 'Qwen-2.5-Math-PRM' baseline here, including the 1.3% law gain in the abstract, is Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct fully fine-tuned on PRM800K, cited to Zheng et al. 2024 (Table 3, p. 24; p. 4). It is not the Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B or -72B of zhang2025prmlessons that EngTrace ran, so the revised text must not say VersaPRM beat 'the Qwen PRM' EngTrace evaluated. The state brief's 'VersaPRM, a LoRA on Llama-PRM800K' matches the paper (p. 6). EngTrace's X1 traces include Llama 3.1 70B outputs, the generator family the authors flag as possibly favoured (p. 9); a per-model breakdown of the VersaPRM result could check this.
